per_shot.note: Chunky faceted amber serpent with a warm halo on the back wall; the head's mouth glow is dim, so the biting end barely outreads the tail at play size.
Segments read clearly and sit in VEIL amber, but they look like hollow cones, and the halo mostly lights empty air, not the tunnel rock it should be burrowing through.
Violet crab reads as a creature with pincers, and its violet pool is self-lit and on-colour, but it floats in an open void and never reads as an ore that bites.
Clean faceted crystal body with a cyan crown and a soft violet bloom; the light pools on the empty backdrop, not on the stone around it.
Cream glowing mannequins merge with the cream pillar and bright core chamber; they read as light but not as a pursuer or a threat.
Washed-out pale bodies with no focal point or menace; sparks are nice, but the silhouette is lost against the lit pillar.
Tight cyan flock with a strong ice-cyan pool landing on the floor; the clearest 'glow that lands' in the set and squarely CRYOS.
Crystalline wings catch the light, and the cyan wash on the floor blocks sells the self-lit flock; individual birds are small but legible.

top_issues.issue: Kindled has no threat read and loses its silhouette in bright scenes
top_issues.why: Pale cream bodies on a cream and amber chamber give no value contrast; a pursuer has to be picked out instantly.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give it a hot focal core and darker or more saturated limbs, or a local darkening behind it, so it separates by value from bright backgrounds.

top_issues.issue: Geode Mimic does not read as an ore
top_issues.why: It hovers in an open cavity as an obvious crab, so the 'ore that bites' fantasy and its tell are absent.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Stage it seated in or against a rock face with a geode-like resting silhouette; let the pincers and legs be the reveal.

top_issues.issue: Creature light lights air more than rock
top_issues.why: The brief wants a creature's light to spill onto the stone around it; here it is mostly a screen-space halo over void.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Stage the Long One and Mimic close enough to rock faces that their point light visibly washes the nearest block faces.

top_issues.issue: Long One's dangerous end is under-stated
top_issues.why: At play size the head glow is about as bright as the body seams, so the eye doesn't go to the mouth.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make the mouth the hottest point on the body, with a stronger value step from head to tail.

protect: Rimewings' cyan floor pool: the creature's own light visibly landing on the rock
Long One's chunky faceted segments in VEIL amber with ember seams
Mimic's violet-on-amber accent with the cyan crystal crown
Low-poly faceted construction across all four

per_shot.note: Same serpent with a white-hot mouth glow; the biting end now clearly leads at play size.
The hot mouth gives a clear focal point and danger read, but the segments are still hollow cones and the light still lands mostly on air.
Crab reads equally well; the cooler, wider pool touches the nearby block faces, but it reads more like headlamp spill than the mimic's own light and still floats in a void.
The tilted pose is more dynamic and the light lands on the right-hand block, but the grey-cyan pool loses A's colour cohesion with the violet body.
Darker bodies with a burning diamond heart, sparks and a local darkening behind them; reads as a figure and a threat against the bright chamber.
Clear silhouettes and a focal heart; the dark smudge aura and dull brown limbs undercut 'made of light' somewhat.
Larger, more bird-like wings and a looser flock, but the cyan floor pool is gone; the floor is lit by the white headlamp only.
Bigger, nicer wing shapes; the flock glows but its light no longer visibly lands on the ice below.

top_issues.why: Without the cyan pool the flock reads as lit objects, not light sources; this is the main way B regresses from A.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Restore a cyan point light or floor wash under the flock, keeping B's larger wing shapes.

top_issues.issue: Kindled's dark aura conflicts with 'a pursuer made of light'
top_issues.why: It solves readability, but a brown body in a dark smudge reads more as shadow than as light.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the heart and value separation, but make the limbs emissive-edged or ember-lit, and keep the darkening subtle or tie it to its glow.

top_issues.issue: Geode Mimic does not read as an ore
top_issues.why: It is shown hovering as an obvious crab with no disguise or tell.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Stage it embedded in or against the rock face with a geode resting silhouette; keep the mimic's light the violet of its body.

top_issues.issue: Long One's segments read as hollow cones, and its light lights air
top_issues.why: The funnel shapes undercut 'serpent', and the halo doesn't wash the tunnel stone.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Close the segment backs or overlap them as plates, and bring the body near rock so the glow lands on the block faces.

protect: Long One's white-hot mouth as the dangerous-end focal point
Kindled's heart-glow focal point and value separation from bright backgrounds
Low-poly faceted construction and world hue families

why: B wins on threat readability: a hot mouth on the Long One and a Kindled that separates from the bright chamber. It gives back A's best moment, the Rimewings' cyan light landing on the floor, so the margin is small.
